technical_body.encoding_rule: Each bit is transmitted as two half-symbols; a transition mid-bit encodes the value.
technical_body.dc_balance: zero-DC (equal high and low time per bit)
technical_body.preamble_typical: 0xAA/0x55 alternating (mid-bit transitions produce a clean clock spike)
canonical_use_cases: OOK keyfobs at 315/433 MHz (rolling code + fixed code)
some weather stations (Acurite 592TXR, Fine Offset WH1080)
technical_body.polarity_recovery: Try both polarity assumptions; the one that yields a valid preamble/CRC wins.

technical_body.encoding_rule: Mid-bit transition always present (for clock recovery). A start-of-bit transition encodes the value.
canonical_use_cases: occasional keyfob variants that resist plain Manchester decoders
technical_body.polarity_recovery: polarity independent — this is the main advantage over plain Manchester.

technical_body.encoding_rule: Level directly encodes the bit for the full symbol period; no mid-bit transition.
technical_body.dc_balance: not DC-balanced; long runs of 0s or 1s produce DC bias
technical_body.clock_recovery: requires a preamble (e.g. 0xAA) or an external clock reference; matched-filter timing recovery on a training sequence.

technical_body.encoding_rule: A transition at the start of a symbol encodes one binary value; no transition encodes the other. Value = XOR of previous level.
technical_body.self_clocking: partial — a long run of 0s (NRZ-mark) has no transitions; requires bit-stuffing (as HDLC does) or preamble.
canonical_use_cases: HDLC / AX.25 packet radio (Bell 202 AFSK-1200, FSK-9600)
technical_body.bit_stuffing_note: HDLC/AX.25 insert a 0 after 5 consecutive 1s to avoid loss of clock; the decoder must strip it before payload assembly.

technical_body.encoding_rule: Each bit is a fixed-period pulse; the ratio of high time to low time within the period encodes the bit.

conventions.short_high_long_low: 0 = short high + long low, 1 = long high + short low
conventions.vendor_variants: polarity and short/long roles are vendor-specific — invert if the preamble misses.

canonical_use_cases: IR remotes (NEC, RC-5, Sony SIRC — same principle over IR carrier)

technical_body.encoding_rule: A short pulse of fixed width; the *gap* between successive pulses encodes the bit value.

conventions.short_gap_long_gap: 0 = short gap, 1 = long gap (or the inverse; polarity is vendor-specific)

canonical_use_cases: ADS-B (Mode S) uses PPM at the bit level: 1 μs slot, first-half high = 1, second-half high = 0

technical_body.encoding_rule: Sample the analog channel at Nyquist rate; represent each sample as an N-bit code word. Not a line code — a *source* code. Here for cross-reference only.
canonical_use_cases: CD audio (16-bit linear PCM at 44.1 kHz)
many digital voice trunks (DMR, TETRA, P25 use vocoders that then feed PCM into a channel code)
technical_body.note: In an RF context, treat PCM as the *content* riding on top of an actual channel code (NRZ, Manchester, …). A decoder rarely sees raw PCM off the air.
